newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva gets two U.S. drug approvals.
newsitem.headline: Teva gets two U.S. drug approvals.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries said on Wednesday it had received approval for two new drugs from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Teva said the FDA had approved a new drug application (NDA) for a proprietary treatment for Wilson's disease, which damages the liver and brain, can cause neurological damage and lead to death. The disease affects about one in 30,000 people.
The product, to be called Galzin, will be marketed by Teva Pharamaceuticals USA Inc, Teva's U.S. subsidiary.
The drug, which was develped at the University of Michigan, was previously designated an "orphan" drug and is therefore protected from competition for its first seven years on the market, Teva said.

The FDA also approved Teva's application for a generic version of ELDEPRYL, a treatment for Parkinson's disease originally developed by the U.S. company Somerset Pharmaceuticals. Teva's generic version will be sold under the name Selegiline.

The company added it was the fourth company to win approval for a generic version of ELDEPRYL. Somerset had annual sales of $100 million from the drug before generic versions were authorised, Teva said.
